title: PCSX2 separates menu navigation from per-game controller profiles
summary: Static FullscreenUI bindings, a DInput exception, corrected XInput detection, and new Nintendo and generic glyph sets make on-screen prompts match the controls that actually navigate the menu.
heroAlt: Visual evidence from PCSX2 pull request #14756: Input/FullscreenUI: Fix shared-binding navigation bug; fix and expand controller icon/glyph support

sourceLabels.pcsx2-pr-14756: Input/FullscreenUI: Fix shared-binding navigation bug; fix and expand controller icon/glyph support

blocks.text: Per-game bindings could disagree with ImGui's fixed prompts

FullscreenUI previously read the active controller profile when deciding which buttons move through ImGui menus. That sounds flexible, but the glyphs displayed by ImGui do not change dynamically with every per-game remap. A profile could therefore make one physical button perform navigation while the screen continued to advertise another. Pull request #14756 removes that mismatch at the point where menu bindings are selected.
SDL and XInput use a static table; DInput remains the exception

PCSX2 now treats menu navigation like a fixed console-style interface for standardized SDL and XInput devices. It deliberately ignores the active game profile, avoiding ambiguous choices when a user creates combo bindings or swaps face buttons. DInput cannot follow the same rule because its button numbering has no standard layout, so that backend continues to resolve the shared global bindings rather than an arbitrary static map.
Controller families now have distinct names and neutral fallback glyphs

The input tables were also separated and corrected. Nintendo controllers gain their own names, including Plus and Minus, while Xbox entries no longer silently reuse the SDL table. XInput's icon conversion now checks for XInput rather than SDL, fixing a condition that previously fell back to PlayStation symbols. A Generic preference supplies shape-neutral glyphs, and SDL devices reported as UNKNOWN use that set unless the user overrides it.
Validation must cross backends, profiles, and unknown devices

The source test plan covers SDL and XInput with a per-game profile active, DInput with shared bindings, Xbox and Nintendo button names in both Qt and ImGui, and the Generic preference. A complete regression pass should also reconnect an unidentified SDL pad and verify that menu actions, displayed glyphs, and the controller-binding screen remain aligned before, during, and after a game-specific profile is enabled.
The important boundary is intentional: gameplay remains remappable per game, while standardized menu navigation stays predictable enough for fixed on-screen glyphs.
